findings.title: Denial cache key ignores identity type, causing cross-identity false denials
findings.body: The denial cache key is built from namespace, UserUID, action, name, and parent, but not IdentityType. validateSubject returns UID "0" for both `anonymous:0` and `render:0` (and potentially other identity types). If an anonymous user is denied access to a dashboard, the negative entry is stored under that key; a subsequent renderer check for the same dashboard/action/parent hits the denial cache and returns false before getCachedIdentityPermissions or getRendererPermissions can grant wildcard read access. This can block rendering of dashboards for up to the cache TTL. Include IdentityType (or otherwise namespace the key per identity type) in userPermDenialCacheKey.

findings.title: Denial cache key concatenation is ambiguous and can collide
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with "_" separators without escaping or length prefixes. Values may themselves contain underscores (for example resource UIDs/folder UIDs), so different tuples can produce the same key, e.g. userUID "a_b", action "c", name "d", parent "e" collides with userUID "a", action "b_c", name "d", parent "e". A collision in the denial cache can cause a user to be denied access to a resource for which no negative decision was actually made. Use an unambiguous encoding (length-prefixed, structured key, or hashed fields).
